text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, even for someone who did not write it. One key habit is following naming conventions, which means choosing clear and meaningful names for variables and functions. Another useful practice is keeping functions small and focused on a single task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Clean code is also easier to maintain, because other developers can quickly find and fix problems. Although writing clean code may take more time at the beginning, it saves a lot of effort later and helps teams work together more effectively.
